title: a birthplace the rule keeps once its words are answered
line: the Massachusetts birth register's Northampton, the record of the birth itself, against the 1940 census's Pennsylvania, secondary information an informant gave: the classes favour the register without doubt, but a place is kept only as a place, so the rule waits on the owner's answer to the register's words and says so; once the words are answered, reconsider resolves the birthplace for Northampton, the event's place is the register's, the census's Pennsylvania stays as the census says it, and the written conclusion prints the resolution with its reason
